title: Codela
excerpt: Production memory for AI coding agents: lessons from the deploys that broke production, so your agents don't repeat them.
content_html:
Production memory
for AI coding agents.

Codela checks every deploy with your monitoring tool. If it made your app slower or caused new errors, Codela writes down what went wrong, and Claude Code, Cursor and Codex read it before touching that code again.

1 · Checks every deploy

Did it get slower? Any new errors?

2 · Writes a lesson

.codela/lessons.md

what broke, and how to avoid it, saved in your repo

3 · Your AI reads it

Claude CodeCursorCodex

before it touches that code again

Start free

See what Codela learns from your repo

Every revert and production fix in your history is a mistake your agents could make again. Codela turns them into rules they follow.

Paste a public repo. Codela reads its last year of reverts and production fixes and shows the lessons your coding agents would get. Public repos only, nothing is written anywhere.

The agent never finds out.

With Codela

The lesson reaches the agent

Codela turns what happened in production into lessons your agents read before their next code change, so the same mistake doesn't ship twice.

Get started

Up and running in minutes

01

Sign in with GitHub

Pick the repos Codela should watch. It reads code and deploys, comments on pull requests and adds lessons to your repo. It only ever writes its own lesson files, never your code.

02

Connect your observability tool

Pick SigNoz, Datadog, Sentry, New Relic or Grafana and paste a read-only key. Codela checks it works and matches your repos to their services. Keys are encrypted.

03

Lessons go into your repo

Right after you connect, Codela checks your last 30 days of deploys and a year of Git history, so you can see what it would have caught before you rely on it. From then on every deploy is checked automatically. Each lesson arrives in your repo as a pull request, and Claude Code, Cursor and Codex read it before they write code. Want to check every lesson first? Switch to review before merge in Settings.

> Show stock levels next to each item in the cart

● Before I write this: Codela has a production lesson for this repo. Calling get_stock() once per cart item made checkout 4× slower after deploy a1b2c3d.

So I'll fetch every item's stock in a single get_stock_many() call, in batches of 50, and pass the results into the cart view.

⎿ Edited checkout/cart.py (+18 −3)

On pull requests

usecodelabotcommented on pull request #214Example

Codela: production lessons

This PR looks like it repeats a mistake this repo already made in production.

Calling inventory-service once per item made checkout 4× slower

Where: checkout/cart.py line 42: get_stock() is called inside a loop over the cart items

Learned from: p95 latency 410ms → 1.7s after deploy a1b2c3d

Why: one checkout request turned into 60+ calls to inventory-service.

Ways to fix:

  • Fetch all items in one call with get_stock_many()
  • Keep batches at 50 items or fewer; the service rejects larger ones

Questions teams ask before they start.

How is this different from Sentry or Datadog alerts?

Alerts tell a person that something broke. Codela works out which code change caused it and turns that into a lesson your coding agents read, so the agent doesn't write the same thing again. It uses the monitoring tool you already have; it doesn't replace it.

Do I have to wait for my next deploy to see anything?

No. When you connect, Codela checks your last 30 days of deploys and reads a year of your Git history (reverts and production fixes), so you see what already broke production, which of those changes came from AI agents, and the lessons it would have written. You can review each lesson before it goes into your repo.

What happens if someone repeats a past mistake?

Codela comments on the pull request with the lesson and the production numbers behind it, so the mistake is caught in review instead of in production.

Can't I just write lessons in CLAUDE.md myself?

You can, but almost nobody does it after every incident, and first you have to work out which change caused the problem. Codela does both automatically after every deploy, with the numbers to back it up.

What if Codela gets a lesson wrong?

It only writes a lesson when it finds that the code change caused the problem, not just that the timing lined up. You can delete any lesson from your dashboard, and it's removed from your repo too.

Does Codela change my code?

Never. The only thing it writes is its lesson files (.codela/lessons.md, plus a line in CLAUDE.md and a section in AGENTS.md), through pull requests. You can turn that off in Settings.

What data does Codela see?

The code changes in the repos you pick, and read-only data from your monitoring tool: speed, error rates, error messages and traces around each deploy. Keys are checked live and stored encrypted, and your lessons are never shown to anyone outside your workspace.

How much does it cost?

Free for 1 repo and 20 pull request checks a month, no card needed. Pro is $7.99 per person per month for unlimited repos, pull request checks and your whole team. Cancel anytime.

How is this different from Sentry or Datadog alerts?

Alerts tell a person that something broke. Codela works out which code change caused it and turns that into a lesson your coding agents read, so the agent doesn't write the same thing again. It uses the monitoring tool you already have; it doesn't replace it.

Do I have to wait for my next deploy to see anything?

No. When you connect, Codela checks your last 30 days of deploys and reads a year of your Git history (reverts and production fixes), so you see what already broke production, which of those changes came from AI agents, and the lessons it would have written. You can review each lesson before it goes into your repo.

What happens if someone repeats a past mistake?

Codela comments on the pull request with the lesson and the production numbers behind it, so the mistake is caught in review instead of in production.

Can't I just write lessons in CLAUDE.md myself?

You can, but almost nobody does it after every incident, and first you have to work out which change caused the problem. Codela does both automatically after every deploy, with the numbers to back it up.

What if Codela gets a lesson wrong?

It only writes a lesson when it finds that the code change caused the problem, not just that the timing lined up. You can delete any lesson from your dashboard, and it's removed from your repo too.

Does Codela change my code?

绝不。 The only thing it writes is its lesson files (.codela/lessons.md, plus a line in CLAUDE.md and a section in AGENTS.md), through pull requests. You can turn that off in Settings.

What data does Codela see?

The code changes in the repos you pick, and read-only data from your monitoring tool: speed, error rates, error messages and traces around each deploy. Keys are checked live and stored encrypted, and your lessons are never shown to anyone outside your workspace.

How much does it cost?

Free for 1 repo and 20 pull request checks a month, no card needed. Pro is $7.99 per person per month for unlimited repos, pull request checks and your whole team. 随时取消。
